name: Dirty bulk / lean bulk

lead: Bulking means eating in a calorie surplus to build muscle. A lean (or clean) bulk uses a small surplus with tracking to limit fat gain, while a dirty bulk uses a large surplus with little tracking, often including processed foods.
On looksmax.org, younger and thinner users ask which approach avoids looking soft or bloated while gaining size. Responses range from small planned surpluses to long continuous bulks.

paras: A surplus supplies energy for tissue growth. Wikipedia says a sustained surplus can add more lean mass than eating at maintenance, with some fat gain expected, and that a larger surplus or longer bulk adds more fat.

Wikipedia describes dirty bulking as producing fast gain but usually significant fat, followed by a harsher cut, with long-term concerns for cardiovascular health and insulin sensitivity. Forum users also report fear of looking fat or bloated.

lead: Bulking is the bodybuilding practice of eating in a calorie surplus to build muscle, usually followed by a cutting phase in a deficit [1]. Wikipedia says competitive bodybuilders spend most of the year in an off-season build and cut for roughly 12 to 14 weeks before a contest [1].

Clean or lean bulking is described as trying to increase muscle without fat gain, using tracking and a controlled surplus, while dirty bulking is a large untracked surplus that can include junk food, giving faster weight gain but usually more fat [1].

On looksmax.org the topic appears as questions from users who want size without looking chubby or bloated [2][3][4][5]. No published trial found tests clean versus dirty bulking for appearance outcomes.

paras: Wikipedia says the link between muscle growth and positive energy balance is well established, and that the size of the surplus depends on the person's goals, since larger surpluses and longer bulks add more fat [1]. It describes clean bulking as relying on tracking such as meeting daily calorie targets and alternating higher and lower days, and dirty bulking as eating a large surplus without tracking macronutrients [1].

Forum threads include a user who asks about a 500-calorie daily surplus to reach a target weight without becoming chubby [2], a teenager asking whether a lean bulk will add fat after a cut [4], users asking whether to clean or dirty bulk [6][7], and threads on bulking after a cut [5][8]. Several posters describe worry about bloating or fat gain altering their facial look, with replies that range from recommending continuous long bulks to suggesting performance-enhancing drugs, which is outside the scope of this article.
No studies found comparing clean and dirty bulking.

lore.intro: Bulk strategy appears on looksmax.org as questions from users who want muscle without fat or facial puffiness [2][3][4][5].

claims.claim: A small, tracked surplus lets you add muscle without getting fat.
Dirty bulking is a faster way to gain size.
